_about: Sculpted column orders and doorway colossi (D-014). Rows in the SITE_SPEC style {v, u, src, tier, note}. Every SHAPE proportion here is tier C: a reconstruction of the type from general knowledge of Achaemenid carving (RECOLLECTION: no measured drawing or scan was available, BLOCKERS B6), fitted to the attested/SITE_SPEC dimensions of each order (height, shaft diameter, flute count, base type, capital type). Unit D = the order's lower shaft diameter (SITE_SPEC); 'fraction of base/capital height' = of the order's baseH/capitalH. Licensed scans or measured drawings would replace these forms (NEEDS #10).

switch.note: technical: camera distance (to a column's axis segment / a colossus centre) beyond which the low-detail mesh is drawn; at 32 m a 10 cm flute spans ~3 px at 1080p and 60 deg, so the V-groove flutes of LOD1 read the same

tessellation.u: segments around / rows [LOD0, LOD1]; crease angles in degrees
tessellation.note: technical: lathe tessellation per LOD and the crease angles above which normals are split (sharp arrises, step edges)

square2.note: square two-stepped plinth under a torus (type IR-PERS, B: Apadana hall bases); step heights C; lower-step width from SITE_SPEC global.r_column_proportions.square2_lower_scale, upper step = the order's baseW

bell.u: fraction of base height (h) / D (r) / fraction of base radius (lip) / profile exponents (radius ∝ (1−t)^flare_pow; rows denser toward the foot)
bell.note: inverted-bell (campaniform) base on a low round foot, torus on top (type IR-PERS, B: porticoes, Gate); bottom radius = half the order's baseW; profile C

bell_leaves.u: count / fraction of bell height / D / fraction of relief / fraction of leaf pitch / fraction of leaf length where the rounded tip begins / fraction of leaf pitch (midrib width; shared by all leaf reliefs)
bell_leaves.note: pendant palm-leaf (petal) band in relief on the bell, tips down, one tier with midribs (motif from photographs of Persepolis bell bases, RECOLLECTION; count, tiers and depth C)

plain.note: low cylindrical drum under a torus (Hadish order, base type C); drum radii from SITE_SPEC global.r_column_proportions.plain_base

torus.u: D / D / count / fraction of flute half-width
torus.note: convex torus under the shaft, carved with horizontal flutes as on Achaemenid bases (RECOLLECTION, C); size C

flutes.u: fraction of flute half-width / D / D
flutes.note: concave flutes meeting in sharp arrises (fluted shafts IR-COL, B; count = SITE_SPEC <building>.flutes); flutes stop short of both ends in rounded terminations, leaving plain bands above the torus and below the capital (RECOLLECTION, C); depth and band heights C. Taper from SITE_SPEC r_column_proportions.shaft_top_ratio

unfluted.note: timber shafts (Treasury) are plaster-sheathed and painted, not fluted (RELIEF-R, B); shafts still under construction (Hall of 100 Columns) are left as unfluted drums because fluting was cut after erection (RECOLLECTION, C)

tessellation.note: technical: samples per flute arc and rows per rounded flute termination

composite_split.note: composite capital bottom to top: drooping-palm bell, upright ribbed calyx, vertical double-volute member, double-bull protome (sequence IR-COL, B; split C). Capital height: SITE_SPEC capital_height where it exists (Apadana 7.8 m), else the same multiple of the shaft diameter (DERIVED, C)

palm.u: D / D / count / D / fraction of member height / leaf length at the rim / profile exponents / leaf half-width, edge softness (fraction of leaf pitch) / midrib height (fraction of relief)
palm.note: inverted bell of drooping palm leaves, tips curling out over the shaft top (RECOLLECTION, C)

calyx.u: D / D / count / D / fraction of member height / profile and rib-section exponents / rib relief at the foot (fraction of the rim relief)
calyx.note: upright calyx with vertical ribs (sepals) flaring to a scalloped rim (RECOLLECTION, C)

bull.u: D / fraction of capital height / D / fraction of the collar height over which it flares from the shaft
bull.note: double-bull capital set on the shaft with a short collar (type IR-PERS, B: Apadana W portico 'double-bull capitals set directly on the fluted shaft'); height 2.2 shaft diameters so the protome keeps the proportions of the composite capital's protome (C)

plain.u: D / fraction of capital height / D
plain.note: Treasury plastered timber posts: plain square bolster under a square abacus of width SITE_SPEC capital_boxes.plain (form not found; C)

frame.note: nominal height of the double-bull protome; width and depth are SITE_SPEC r_column_proportions.capital_boxes.protome (3.4 x 1.1 D); the unit mesh is fitted to each order's box (the beam runs along grid x, C)

body.u: D (x along the beam, bull facing +x, mirrored; y up from the protome base)
body.note: two addorsed bull forequarters joined at the back, a flat saddle between the necks where the main beam sits (type IR-COL, B; masses RECOLLECTION, C)

head.note: stylised bull head held forward, muzzle down, horns curving up and forward, ears out (RECOLLECTION, C)

legs.note: forelegs folded under the chest, knees forward, hooves tucked back (kneeling pose of Persepolis capital bulls, RECOLLECTION, C)

curls.note: rows of curled locks as relief bands on the dewlap/chest front and a forelock tuft between the horns (RECOLLECTION, C); curls are modelled as bosses (their spiral is below the mesh resolution)

mc.note: technical: marching-cubes cells (LOD0, LOD1), simplification targets, crease angle for normals

member.u: fraction of member width (relief, scroll_r) / fraction of member height (scroll_r_max) / fraction of scroll radius (eye, fill) / D
member.note: tall member with, on each of the four faces, two stacked pairs of spiral scrolls (top pair curling down, bottom pair curling up) joined by vertical stems, a reeded band between them (double volutes IR-COL, B; carving RECOLLECTION, C). Cross-section = SITE_SPEC capital_boxes.volute (1.25 x 0.9 D)

reference_box.note: the model is authored in metres in this box (= SITE_SPEC gate_nations.r_colossus when written) and scaled to the current r_colossus box

jamb.note: colossus carved from the doorway jamb: the fore-part stands in the round in front of the jamb block (as far as the colossus box projects beyond the wall face), the flank is high relief on the passage face of the block, whose background is cut back by relief_depth inside a back and top frame (Achaemenid/Assyrian gate-colossus type, RECOLLECTION, C)

body.u: m (reference box; x along the body, head +x; y above the plinth; z relative to the body's median plane zc, +z = passage side)
body.note: standing bull body, massive and smoothly modelled (bulls W, human-headed winged bulls E: IR-PERS, B; proportions RECOLLECTION, C)

legs.u: m (z relative to the leg's own plane zc ± dz)
legs.note: four legs: the forelegs standing side by side in the round, the hind legs striding in relief (C: the leg count of the Persepolis gate colossi was not verified)

bull_head.u: m (reference box, z relative to zc)
bull_head.note: W doorway bulls (IR-PERS/ISAC, B): bull head facing out of the doorway, horns up and forward (form RECOLLECTION, C)

human_head.u: m (reference box, z relative to zc)
human_head.note: E doorway: bearded human head (IR-PERS/ISAC, B: 'human-headed winged bulls', bearded, horned tiara), long square beard of curls, hair mass behind, bull ears with earrings (form RECOLLECTION, C)

crown.note: cylindrical horned tiara (RELIEF-R §2, B for the horned tiara): three horn pairs as bands wrapping the cylinder, a crest of upright ribs at the top (details C)

wing.note: wing (RELIEF-R §2, B: winged) rising from the shoulder along the back to the rear top of the relief field: covert scales in front, long primaries behind (form RECOLLECTION, C)

curls.note: rows of curls as bosses: chest and dewlap, belly fringe, forelock (bull), beard and hair (lamassu) (RECOLLECTION, C)
